dedupe_keys.name: forecasting demand data for critical materials bass diffusion projections for gallium indium and cobalt to 2050 nist

description: This dataset gives demand projections to 2050 for three critical materials, gallium, indium and cobalt, produced with the Bass diffusion model. For each metal there is an Excel workbook with historical global production, the fitted Bass coefficients p and q, and average, high and low demand scenarios, plus a Jupyter notebook with the coded model and graphs of historical production and demand. It was prepared by Kyle Foster of Miami University and Nehika Mathur of the National Institute of Standards and Technology and described in a data article published on 9 October 2024. Coverage is global annual totals from about 2006, with projections to 2050. The article is open access under CC BY 4.0 and the files are in the NIST Public Data Repository, free to download. Caveats: the authors note that market-specific demand data for critical materials are very limited, so the projections rest on production series used as a proxy for demand and on a diffusion curve fitted to them. For simulation it provides demand paths for metals used in solar panels, batteries and electronics, for supply risk and capacity scenarios of energy and industrial supply chains. It is related to the multicommodity supply curve model record in this catalogue, which simulates supply and prices for cobalt. Licence (read on 2026-09-29): NIST data licence (https://www.nist.gov/open/license, cited in the repository record).
